title: Introduction
text: Hi, I'm Aishwarya from the team. This video covers turning the patent agent CLI into a real callable web API and a real Git mistake that briefly cost the whole file. One new file. One Git

title: The Real Loss
text: Command later, it was gone. Not because the code was wrong, because it was never actually committed. Method, the CLI

title: Why an API, Not Just the CLI
text: Works, but it only works from a terminal. A real HTTP endpoint means any client, a browser, a front end, another service can ask for a patent reading the same way without shelling out to Python directly. The API doesn't re-implement

title: Wrapping the Same, Already-Verified Logic
text: Anything. One route, one publication number in, the same claims agent and lineage agent that were already tested through the CLI called the same way. A real classify flag, same purpose as the CLI's no classify option. Skip the one part that always costs something real. Mid-build, a Git pull failed

title: The Real Mistake
text: Diverged branches, a forced update on the remote. Fixing that meant resetting the local main and rebasing the work branch on top of it. The rebase succeeded. The uncommitted new file didn't survive it. It was staged, not committed, and the branch switched during the fix wiped it out. The real

title: What Actually Protected the Work
text: File wasn't lost for good because the same content still existed locally outside Git from building and testing it minutes earlier. Recreated, committed immediately this time, verified again against the same two real patents that had already confirmed the CLI was correct. Checking the readme before committing turned up

title: A Second Real Find, While Fixing the First
text: Something else. An earlier real update documenting the lineage agent's broader testing had never actually made it into the main branch at all. Fixed in the same pass, not left for later. Your turn. Before switching

title: Your Turn: Check git status First
text: Branches or resetting anything in Git, run Git status first. A file that's staged but not committed can disappear the moment you check out somewhere else and it won't warn you. From Clyde to API
